Enumerate the finite response histories lexicographically using the fixed response list in [F1], and partition F_{i-1} into its positive-probability histories h. By [A1], each satisfies Pr(C_q(Y_i)=0|h)<=1-p, so finite additivity gives Pr(F_i)=sum_h Pr(h)Pr(C_q(Y_i)=0|h)<=(1-p)Pr(F_{i-1}). Induction from Pr(F_0)=1 yields Pr(F_N)<=(1-p)^N.

For each draw let B_i={A_q(Y_i)=1,C_q(Y_i)=0}. Any accepted incorrect output selected from the N candidates lies in union_i B_i. For every outcome, 1_{union_i B_i}<=sum_i 1_{B_i}; summing this pointwise inequality against the nonnegative finite outcome masses gives Pr(union_i B_i)<=sum_i Pr(B_i)<=N epsilon. Thus the false-acceptance probability is at most N epsilon. No factorization or independence is used in this step.
